source.title: Preserving Privacy in GANs Against Membership Inference Attack
source.authors: Mohammadhadi Shateri; Francisco Messina; Fabrice Labeau; Pablo Piantanida

record.tranche_reason: Measures discriminator generalization gaps and membership inference in GANs, extending generalization-gap analysis to generative models and privacy attacks; it does not test the listed classifier versions.
record.gate_note: The paper reports GAN discriminator gaps, score overlap, memorization ratios, membership-inference accuracy, and synthetic-data utility. It does not test random-label fitting, classifier test error on natural labels, or any of V1–V8's specified interventions or measures.
record.test_reason: The study measures GAN discriminator score distributions, membership inference, nearest-neighbor memorization, and synthetic-data utility. None tests V1–V8. Shared terms such as generalization gap and memorization do not establish a match: there are no random-label experiments, width sweeps, convolutional versus fully connected comparisons, optimizer or batch comparisons, dropout ablations, weight-perturbation measures, or removal of memorized examples.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors propose discriminator score overlap as a more complete overfitting measure than a mean score gap, report that MEGAN and MIMGAN reduce membership-inference accuracy toward their random-attack reference, and acknowledge fidelity/diversity trade-offs. They emphasize MIMGAN's adjustable privacy–utility trade-off through lambda.
record.recipe_differences: Studies GAN discriminator overfitting and membership-inference attacks, using proposed entropy and mutual-information objectives; it does not use the classifier training recipes in the listed claim versions.
record.method_sensitivity: Discriminator architecture changes measured generalization gap, score overlap, and MIA accuracy; MIMGAN’s lambda changes score overlap and MIA accuracy. Dataset and privacy method also vary across reported results.

fits_no_version.finding: On MNIST, simplifying the discriminator reduces its score gap from 0.55 to 0.03 and membership-inference accuracy from 60.37% to 31.91%, still above the study's 10% random reference. MIMGAN increases score overlap while the MNIST mean gap remains around 0.03–0.04.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In these GAN experiments, discriminator score-distribution overlap captures membership-inference vulnerability beyond the difference in mean scores.

fits_no_version.finding: Table III reports substantially lower attack accuracy for MEGAN and MIMGAN than vanilla GAN, with lower reported classifier utility. Their reported utility exceeds PrivGAN and DP-GAN on both datasets.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The proposed GAN privacy objectives offer an empirical privacy–utility trade-off on MNIST and fashion-MNIST; Table III's utility evaluation direction requires clarification.

record.problems: No uncertainty estimates are reported. The results concern GAN discriminator scores and membership-inference attacks, not classifier test error on natural or random labels. The text states that the Chest X-Ray and Anime Faces results are in the appendix; corresponding tables are present in the supplied text.
record.rows_left_out: None. Table III comparator results are retained; figure-only precision and recall values from Fig. 7 are omitted because no numerical values are stated in the text.

untested.parts: All: fitting fixed random labels and comparing held-out classification on natural versus random labels.
All: widening beyond zero training error and measuring subsequent test error.
All: convolutional versus fully connected classifier generalization and the contribution of local connectivity.
All: adaptive versus SGD optimizer generalization under specified tuning budgets and remedies.
All: batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and adapted training recipes.
All: dropout's effect on held-out classifier error. Architectural use and background discussion of dropout provide no ablation.
All: magnitude-aware weight sharpness, correlation with generalization gaps, and comparison with norm- and margin-based measures.
All: influence-based identification and removal of memorized training examples, retraining, and comparison with random removal.

record.verdict_notes: All row states are cannot_determine relative to V1–V8 because the measures do not test those versions; this does not dispute the reported GAN/privacy effects. Each row bundles several measures that would require separate rows if retained for a different claim. No additional results bearing on V1–V8 were found in the supplied text.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and held-out classification accuracy on natural versus random labels.
Width sweeps and test error beyond the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected classifier generalization.
Adaptive optimizer versus SGD generalization comparisons.
Large versus small batch generalization under epoch budgets.
Dropout's effect on classifier test error.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its ranking against norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing memorized training examples and measuring resulting test accuracy.
